avoid_when: Most useful information is in the ordered item sequence rather than tabular field interactions.
Feature dimensions or categorical vocabularies are so sparse that extra cross capacity overfits despite regularization.
candidates.summary: Augment an embedding-plus-MLP scorer with a small Deep & Cross Network branch so that user, video, context, popularity, and history fields receive explicit bounded-degree crosses alongside nonlinear deep interactions.
candidates.title: Deep & Cross ranker for bounded-order feature interactions
use_when: Interactions such as user-by-category affinity, video-by-context, and recency-by-history-length are expected to matter.
You want controlled explicit crosses without enumerating manual feature conjunctions.
The embedding-plus-MLP baseline has useful signal but leaves room for better GAUC or nDCG@5.

avoid_when: Most training groups are homogeneous, because they yield no valid positive-negative pairs.
Cross-user negatives would be needed to create pairs; these are misaligned with within-user scoring.
Pair enumeration is too large and negative sampling cannot be made deterministic.
candidates.summary: Construct preference pairs only within the same displayed user candidate group, with a positive long-view impression preferred to a negative one, and optimize logistic score differences. Sample a bounded number of negatives per positive to control cost while directly training the ordering used by GAUC.
candidates.title: Within-user RankNet pairwise ranking loss
use_when: Validation GAUC is the limiting metric and mixed-label user groups are sufficiently common.
The model can batch impressions by user candidate group.
A ranking-focused alternative to pointwise BCE is required without listwise softmax instability.

avoid_when: The sole objective must explicitly prioritize top-five swaps and a stable pointwise baseline has already plateaued.
Labels are missing or are not available for every scored training impression.
candidates.summary: Train the long-view logit with numerically stable binary cross-entropy, weighting each impression inversely by its user candidate-count so prolific users do not dominate a GAUC-style within-user objective. Use this as the low-variance reference objective and preserve raw probabilities for diagnostics.
candidates.title: User-normalized pointwise binary cross-entropy
use_when: A reliable first neural-ranker objective is needed under scarce experiment budget.
The scorer needs a stable supervised signal on every labeled impression.
Candidate lists contain many zero/mixed/all-positive groups, making pure ranking losses partially undefined or uninformative.

avoid_when: The dataset is small enough that quantization adds engineering risk without a meaningful resource benefit.
Low-precision kernels are unavailable or prediction parity cannot be verified on the target hardware.
Rare-entity ranking quality is a primary concern and dequantization error is concentrated in those rows.
candidates.summary: Keep infrequent embedding rows in low precision and retain a bounded full-precision cache for the most frequently accessed training entities. Use per-row scale metadata, a deterministic cache rule based only on training frequencies, and verify score drift before accepting the memory reduction.
candidates.title: Quantized embedding tables with a full-precision hot-row cache
use_when: Embedding-table and optimizer-state memory limits batch size, model width, or feasible architecture choices.
Frequent entities dominate accesses and a compact deployment artifact is required.
The runtime supports tested low-precision embedding lookup on the intended Windows/Linux target.

avoid_when: The validation result shows that a candidate-specific reading of behavioral history is consistently valuable.
A simple model already saturates both GAUC and nDCG@5 and scarce experiments are better spent on objective or feature changes.
candidates.summary: A compact pointwise scorer that concatenates user/video ID embeddings, metadata embeddings, causal history features, and numeric aggregates before a residual MLP outputs one long-view logit per impression.
candidates.title: Embedding-plus-MLP pointwise ranker
use_when: A strong, low-risk architecture baseline is needed before adding specialized interaction or sequence modules.
Candidate lists are short and scoring every displayed impression independently is computationally inexpensive.
You need an architecture that cleanly accommodates all causally available dense and categorical features.

avoid_when: Candidate groups are predominantly size one or have no mixed labels.
The implementation cannot compute group-local ranks and swap deltas without leakage across groups.
Experiment budget cannot support a controlled coefficient comparison against the BCE parent.
required_features: candidate position only for training-group reconstruction
candidates.summary: Combine user-normalized binary cross-entropy with a within-user pairwise logistic term weighted by the absolute nDCG@5 change induced by swapping each positive-negative pair. Start with BCE-dominant weighting and tune one fixed ranking-loss coefficient, targeting top-five order without discarding broad GAUC supervision.
candidates.title: BCE plus LambdaRank-style nDCG@5 hybrid
use_when: nDCG@5 trails GAUC or top-ranked errors are the principal failure mode.
Candidate groups have at least some positive-negative pairs and usually exceed one candidate.
A compact metric-aligned change can be tested on top of an established BCE model.

avoid_when: Candidate-specific history attention or complex feature crosses have already shown a clear validated gain worth their added cost.
The target depends primarily on nonlinear context interactions that a shallow residual cannot recover.
required_features: impression-time context and numeric features; optional
candidates.summary: Use a compact user–video dot product as the main affinity score, then add a small linear or one-hidden-layer residual head for causal numeric, metadata, and context features. This provides a materially cheaper comparator to MLP and attention rankers while preserving personalized score variation.
candidates.title: Dot-product ranker with a small linear residual head
use_when: A fast, low-variance baseline is needed before spending scarce experiments on deeper rankers.
The deployment path may later require efficient batched scoring or approximate inner-product retrieval.
User and video ID embeddings carry substantial predictive signal.

avoid_when: Slice deficits are based on tiny supports or are not stable under paired group bootstrap.
The optimization budget cannot support tracking per-group moving losses and weights.
The intended groups encode protected attributes without an approved fairness and governance protocol.
required_features: predeclared training-only temporal, frequency, history-depth, or group-size assignments
ordinary user-normalized BCE or within-group ranking anchor
candidates.summary: Optimize a robust mixture of group-complete ranking losses by upweighting predeclared high-loss groups, such as late training periods, sparse-history users, rare videos, or candidate-group-size buckets. Combine the group-DRO term with strong regularization and early stopping, because worst-group optimization alone can overfit neural models; retain the ordinary objective as an anchor to protect the primary aggregate metric. ([mlanthology.org](https://mlanthology.org/iclr/2020/sagawa2020iclr-distributionally/?utm_source=openai))
candidates.title: Predeclared group-DRO within-user ranking objective
use_when: Temporal and population-slice evaluation reveals repeatable regressions despite acceptable aggregate GAUC and nDCG@5.
A model is suspected of exploiting correlations concentrated in frequent entities or historical periods.
Predeclared groups have enough complete mixed-label candidate groups to estimate stable losses.

avoid_when: The target is driven mainly by stable user-video affinity and histories are mostly sparse.
Event timestamps are tied or unreliable enough that causal ordering cannot be implemented safely.
Scarce experiment budget cannot support checking sequence length, dropout, and attention-width sensitivity.
candidates.summary: Encode each user's strictly pre-impression video sequence with a lightweight causal self-attention encoder, combine its last-state representation with the candidate video and context embeddings, and score the displayed impression with a shallow head.
candidates.title: Causal self-attentive sequence encoder ranker
use_when: Timestamp ordering is reliable and sequential transitions or evolving interests are likely to add signal beyond aggregates.
Users have enough prior interactions for sequence modeling after causal truncation.
You can cap history length and use a small transformer to keep training and inference practical.

avoid_when: never replace fixed evaluation
candidates.summary: Explains official and advisory metrics, their weighting, tradeoffs, and interpretation hazards.
candidates.title: Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics
use_when: diagnosing every scored experiment
predicting metric-specific effects

avoid_when: Most users have extremely short or empty usable histories.
Per-candidate attention creates unacceptable inference cost relative to the small expected gain.
History items lack informative IDs or attributes after leakage-safe truncation.
candidates.summary: Use a Deep Interest Network-style local activation module to pool a causally truncated user history differently for every candidate video, then fuse the candidate-aware interest vector with ID, metadata, and aggregate inputs in a final scorer.
candidates.title: Candidate-conditioned behavioral-history attention ranker
use_when: Users have heterogeneous histories in which only a subset of prior videos is relevant to a candidate.
The same user receives diverse video candidates, making a single fixed user-history vector too coarse.
Causal recent-video IDs and associated attributes are available at impression time.
